## 2026-11-12 - Code review: bubbles on short files placed beside the code again
Found by test_patcher once patch 0011 was the newest: on a file whose review is short enough that the code viewer shows no scroll bar, the hidden scroll bar still reported the viewer's whole width (1,036 px). ## 2026-11-12 - Exit fixed; Esc closes menus everywhere
Asked: "exit button seems to be bugged when i press esc, use esc key to exit menus as shortcut".

**The bug.** Talos's Exit did nothing once you had opened the Library or Versions. exit() checked each tool's unsaved changes with `bool(n.get("dirty"))`; those two tools have no `dirty`, so it called `bool(null)`, a script error in Godot 4, and stopped. It now checks `n.get("dirty") == true`.

**Talos.**
- Esc on any Talos screen now does what Exit does: it leaves to the title screen, asking about unsaved work tool by tool.
- Each tool's own Esc steps still come first: deselect, finish a pen path, leave a Library room for the browser.
- Before, Esc in a tool went to the Dialogue page.
- The Exit tooltip shows [Esc].
- Versions marks Esc handled before leaving (it called set_input_as_handled on a freed viewport).

**In the game.** Esc used to open the Esc menu over any open window ("Esc never closes this window"). Now Esc closes the open window first, and Esc again opens the Esc menu. This covers:
- the Ship Computer (every tab, the maps included);
- the Field Computer;
- the surface map;
- the station menu (Esc undocks, as the Undock button; its tooltip says so);
- the Level Editor (Esc exits, as F10).

The dialogue box keeps Esc for the Esc menu. The pause menu already closed its sub-panels (settings, save slots, CRT) on Esc, then resumed.

Checked: every Talos screen exits on Esc and on Exit, after all tools have been opened. Every Ship Computer tab closes on Esc; the station menu closes on Esc; the slots and pause behave. Tests: 226 pass.

Files: scripts/editor_screen.gd, talos_nav.gd, scenario_editor.gd, svg_editor.gd, patcher.gd, zoo.gd, ship_menu.gd, field_menu.gd, surface_map.gd, station_menu.gd, level_editor.gd, ui.gd; data/docs/editor.md, game.md.

## 2026-11-12 - A short label beside every icon, everywhere (Library first)
Asked: "in library add relevant text next to icons, try to keep the label short and concise, make sure in this regard the ui is uniform among all areas including outside talos". (Interrupted by the Esc fix and Kilon's conversation; resumed after the power cut.)

**One rule, in one place.** EditorIcons.dress() - which every icon button in Talos and the game goes through - used to make a button icon-only, its name in the tooltip. Now it shows the icon and a short label beside it.
- The label is the `label` argument, or short_label(tooltip). short_label tries, in order:
  - a SHORT table for long titles ("Save to file" -> Save, "Documentation" -> Help, "Close the Ship Computer" -> Close, "Centre on your ship" -> My ship, "Zoom to page" -> Fit page...);
  - a SHORT_PREFIX table for titles made at run time ("Land on Amnissos" -> Land, "Plot route to X" -> Plot route);
  - the title itself if it's 14 characters or fewer;
  - else its first two words, never ending on a word like "and" or "the" ("Select and transform" -> Select).
- The full name, keys and help stay in the tooltip.
- EditorIcons.action() buttons (the stations' buy, sell and fit) show their verb and number: "Buy 600" instead of "600".

**The Library.**
- Its categories show their icon and name.
- The room tabs show their icon and a short name (People, Ships, Stations, Planets, Rocks, Suns, Nebulae, Buildings, Effects, GUI, Monsters). They use the plain font and tighter padding, so eleven fit the bar.
- Browser, Reset view and Help are labelled; the LIBRARY title's margins are trimmed.

**Elsewhere** (the same rule, checked in screenshots):
- Talos's headers (Preview, Save, Reload, Help...) and the dialogue rows' Up / Down / Delete;
- the SVG tools (Select, Edit nodes, Rectangle, Ellipse, Star, Pen, Pencil, Text, Colour picker) and its toolbar (New ... Snap, Help);
- the Ship Computer (Guide, Close) and its map (Routes, Whole map, My ship);
- the galaxy map's Plot route / Clear;
- the stations (Guide, Undock, Buy ...);
- the HUD's death panel (Respawn, Load, Menu) and the dialogue box (Skip, Continue).

**Esc in the hints.** The close buttons' tooltips and the Ship / Field Computer and surface map hints now mention Esc (it closes them since the Esc change).

**Tests and frame rate.**
- test_editor: every icon button has its icon, a label of two words at most, and a full tooltip.
- test_frontier: the Library's categories have an icon and their name.
- 226 pass.
- FPS tour: 91 scenarios, none under 240 average. Two signal sites each had one frame over 50 ms on the first run after the reboot (cold caches); their rerun: all 7 pass, worst frame 17 ms.

Docs: editor.md (buttons show an icon and a short name; the Library's categories and rooms).

## 2026-11-12 - A loading screen for loading a save
Asked: "loading a save has no loading screen". Before, Load froze the menu (one long frame rebuilding the galaxy), then for a save made on a planet the surface built behind a black fade - about 7 s with nothing saying what was happening.

Done:
- New LoadVeil (scripts/load_veil.gd): a full-screen layer (128) in the start-up loading screen's look - "LOADING SLOT 1" / "LOADING QUICKSAVE" / "LOADING AUTOSAVE", the neon bar, the stage under it ("Restoring the galaxy", then "Landing on Amnissos"). It shows, waits two frames so it's on screen before the long frame, then changes scene under it.
- The bar: 30% for the space scene, the rest follows the surface's build_progress. It closes (0.3 s fade) once a *new* game scene is ready - SaveGame.travelling back to false, and a surface built - three frames later; 30 s timeout as a safety net. It only counts a scene other than the one the load started from, so loading from the in-game Esc menu doesn't close it at once. It takes the clicks while up.
- SaveGame.load_slot(slot) is now the one way to load: the title screen / Esc menu's Load list (main_menu._load_from), the death panel's Load (hud._on_load) and F9 quickload all go through it. A second load while one is under way is ignored.
- Measured: a planet save loads in ~7 s, the veil up the whole time (screenshots: galaxy, landing at 30-75%, fade into the surface). Also checked loading from inside a running game.

Tests: test_saves.test_loading_screen (no save: no veil; up while loading; takes clicks; gone when the space scene is ready; on a planet: the bar follows the build, names the planet, gone when built). 226 pass (test_bouncer_plasma flaked once, passes alone).

Docs: game.md (saving: the loading screen).

Files: scripts/load_veil.gd (new), scripts/save_game.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, scripts/hud.gd, tests/test_saves.gd, data/docs/game.md.

## 2026-11-13 - The empires' stories, Kilon Alios on every world, the empires' buildings
Asked (an hour alone): run tests and improve benchmarks; main quests for every empire, at least 3 hours in all, each reflecting the empire's culture and history in a sci-fi setting, with other Greek gods, faithful to the myths and to how the ancient Greeks told stories (no modernisation, easy English); then: placeholder buildings and furniture per empire (Minoan style as a guide, each culture's own, procedural so they can be redesigned); then: Kilon Alios on every planet, telling the history and culture of each empire and of all New Hellas, the narrator of the stories.

Frame rate (quiet machine): 89 / 91 scenarios at 240+ (the Selene Field Computer's 1 s freezes earlier were the other game); the Thalassa wolf-pack fight is borderline (p95 3.3-5.1 ms run to run - noise; A/B with the text hook off showed no difference); surface tour after everything: 32 / 32 at 240+.

Scenario engine (quests across systems never strand):
- Spawn records (Scenarios state "spawns": group, ship type, place, left, system): ships ordered for a place in another system come out when you get there; ships left alive when you jump away come back when you return (ScenarioHost.spawn_pending on arrival); each ship tagged with its record (quest_tag scenario:id:group:record) so losses count. Same for dropped items ("drops"; taken ones not dropped again) and markers (a named place's marker attaches to the system that has it).
- Old hosts without spawn_pending still work (fallback to spawn / drop_item).
- Old saves get scenarios added later (load_save_data starts enabled ones missing from the save).

The empires' main quests (tools/empire_quests.py -> data/scenarios.json "empire_*", lore into data/main_quest.json):
- Athens, The Olive and the Owl (8 steps): Athena's olive withers - the bronze owl at Laurion, thieves at Sounion, offerings to Poseidon at Piraeus, the trident returned, the narrows before the Ugarit gate (Salamis), the raider chief, a timed run to Athenai (Marathon).
- Sparta, With Your Shield or On It (9): the agoge trial, the oracle "love of money will destroy Sparta", the exile Leotychidas sold the gate codes, Thermopylai held in three waves, the Twin Stars relit, Cerberus at Tainaron.
- Mycenae, The Mask of Gold (9): the stolen gold mask, Brontes the Cyclops-engine, the walls mended, the Hydra of Lerna, Artemis stills the gates as at Aulis (the hind), the thieves at Pylos, Cetus.
- Ionia, The First Principle (8): the eclipse foretold, the Panionion council, Theano's instrument, Herostratos burns Artemis's temple for fame (and his name is forbidden), a timed race before the eclipse, Skylla in the dark, the singer Melesigenes (Homer).
- Cyclades, The Wandering Isle (8): Delos drifts from its four pillars as before Leto's labour - Siphnos's honest tithe, Melos's obsidian, Paros's marble, Ariadne's crown on Naxos, Echidna sent by Hera, the pillars raised, the rite of broken figures on Keros.
- 42 steps, 103 rules, 12 encyclopedia entries; each begins at its capital, opens "Sing, Muse...", is told by Kilon Alios; bosses are the game's own monsters (Cerberus, Hydra, Cetus, Skylla, Echidna). Estimated 35-45 minutes each (several jumps, 3-4 fights and a boss, 2-3 deliveries): over 3 hours with the Minoan story.
- Voiced: tools/voice_lines.py now reads scenario dialogue and Kilon's new topics; new speakers mapped to the voices; Greek names' pronunciations. 303 lines (was 99), 15.1 MB.

Kilon Alios on every world (planet_surface.gd, QuestData.GIVER "empires" / "hellas"):
- He stands by every landing pad (the quest's triangle only on Amnissos). Away from home: "Who are you?", three topics on the people holding the world (who they are, their gods, their great deeds - Minoans, Athenians, Spartans, Mycenaeans, Ionians, Islanders; one each for the Sea Peoples' and free worlds), and five on New Hellas (how it began, who built the gates - Ephestos, why the empires quarrel, where the gods are now, the Atrapos sector). He narrates the empire quests.

The empires' buildings (placeholders, procedural):
- Materials: BuildingLook TEMPLATES mycenaean, ionian, cycladic (athenian, spartan existed); a planet takes its owner's look (EMPIRE_LOOK) when no theme preset says otherwise. Buildings named for their people ("Athenian palace").

## 2026-11-13 - Sparta redesigned: its own procedural buildings, furniture and people
Asked: "why this building i am located looks so minoan?" then "no i asked you for a completely redesign with new procedural sprites, spartans also use their own sprites, they have a t-rex head instead of triceratops". The first pass only recoloured the Minoan art (and Sparta's red-and-bronze barely differs from it) and dressed rooms with a few code-drawn pieces - the buildings were still the Minoan painted tiles. Now Sparta has its own, drawn procedurally; the other empires follow the same way.

Buildings - tools/empire_tiles.py (new), data/sprites/tile_spa_*.png (37 pieces):
- A toolkit (stone courses with grain and per-block tint, bands, round shields, isometric diamonds with uv patterns - flags, borders, meander, Laconian roof tiles, sheet metal - shaded cylinders, standing pieces) and a culture spec (colours, course height, block sizes, motifs, pieces); redesign = edit the spec, run again.
- Walls are drawn as a flat front view 112 x 216 (exactly one storey for MinoanTiles._compose_wall, which samples columns and slants them onto the wall line); floors / roofs as the 2:1 top diamond (_compose_diamond); standing pieces anchored at their bottom centre.
- Sparta: grey limestone in heavy courses, a scarlet plinth and cornice; walls plain, with rows of bronze lambda shields, a lambda band, relief spears, and the inscription "ΜΟΛΩΝ ΛΑΒΕ"; fortress slit windows; a bronze-bound door; grey flagstones, packed earth, black-and-scarlet mosaics, a scarlet meander; Laconian terracotta roofs, bronze sheet, flat stone; fluted Doric columns with a scarlet band; roof crowns - a great crested helmet, a bronze tripod, a spear-mast with a pennant, corner blocks; decor - a hoplite statue, tripods, stacks of shields, spear racks, a training post, braziers, lambda banners. (The other orientation's walls are drawn darker, not mirrored, so the writing reads right.)
- MinoanTiles: STYLES sparta_palace / sparta_warehouse / sparta_temple; MinoanTiles.culture (set by PlanetSurface while it builds, cleared on exit): style("palace") resolves to "sparta_palace" when the culture has one - buildings keep their base style everywhere else (furniture lists, temple names). CAP_WALL spa.
- Fixed on the way: a style with fewer than 3 caps broke the roof crown (index error) - the Spartan warehouse / temple; and a double comma in STYLES that broke every surface (caught in the test window).

People - tools/empire_citizens.py (new), art/spartan/ (16 frames: idle and aim, 8 views):
- From the Minoan guard's sheets: each frame's triceratops head and frill cut at the neck (the narrowest row between frill and shoulders), a tyrannosaur head drawn in its place facing the same way (profile, three-quarter, front, back) - bronze plates, amber eye, teeth, a scarlet horsehair crest along the skull like a hoplite's helmet - drawn 3x, lit from above, speckled with scales, outlined dark like the painted bodies, shrunk smooth; the body recoloured (cream ceramic -> iron, gold -> bronze, bright reds -> scarlet).
- surface_props.gd CULTURE_CITIZENS: on a world the culture holds every citizen is one of its people - Sparta: the "spartan" rig, "Spartan hoplite", Spartan names (Brasidas, Lysandros, Gorgo, Kyniska...).

Furniture - tools/empire_furniture.py (new), art/furniture/sparta/ (44 pictures + anchors.json):
- Isometric boxes, cylinders and flat shapes in the game's projection at the pictures' scale (Furniture.ART_K), lit like the vault; two facings mirrored. Every picture the furniture uses, in Spartan forms: mess-hall tables, folding stools with sheepskins, a stone seat with the lambda, reed beds (Spartans slept on rushes), an iron-bound cupboard, black-glazed Laconian jars, the black-broth cauldron, barley loaves, Artemis Orthia's wooden figure, the scytale rods, spear-and-shield racks, iron consoles and lockers, a scarlet rug...
- Furniture.picture(): a culture's own picture when it has one (anchors per folder).

## 2026-11-13 - Athens, Mycenae, Ionia and the Cyclades redesigned (buildings, furniture, people)
Asked: "RESUME any uncomplete tasks" - the redesign done for Sparta, now for every other empire; and the event log's "Scenario started" noise.

Buildings - tools/empire_tiles.py (data/sprites/tile_ath_* 37, tile_myc_* 34, tile_ion_* 37, tile_cyc_* 33):
- Athens: Pentelic marble courses; walls with a Doric frieze (triglyphs, painted metopes), the blue Panathenaic procession, a meander, Athena's owl between olive sprays, a decree "ΕΔΟΞΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ"; tall windows with blue shutters; veined marble floors, black-and-white pebble mosaics (owl, rosette, meander border); Attic terracotta and marble roofs; white Doric columns; a pediment crown, palmette acroteria, Athena Promachos (the gilded spear-tip); herms, decree steles, Panathenaic prize amphorae, owls, olive trees, theatre masks.
- Mycenae: Cyclopean masonry - a new generator, huge irregular boulders (nearest-centre polygons, dark joints); bands of spirals and rosettes, the Lion Gate's lions, a chariot fresco, gold; a relieving triangle over every door; small windows under heavy lintels; painted grid floors with an octopus (as at Pylos); flat earthen roofs; columns tapering downwards with round capitals; the lions as roof crown, a tholos (beehive tomb) dome; the gold death-mask on a stand, a boar's-tusk helmet, chariot wheels, oxhide ingots, the Cyclops's anvil, stirrup jars.
- Ionia: marble with lapis and gold; egg-and-dart, palmettes (anthemion), a star chart, Herakleitos's "ΠΑΝΤΑ ΡΕΙ", the squares of Pythagoras, a vine trellis; gold-framed lapis windows; blue-and-white checker, marble, a gold sun mosaic; blue glazed tiles and garden roofs; Ionic columns with volutes; an armillary sphere, an observatory dish, Anaximander's sundial (gnomon), lyres, a seated sage, planters.
- The Cyclades: smooth whitewash (a new generator, no courses); running spirals (the Syros "frying pans"), an engraved longboat, a niche with a folded-arm figure, an obsidian band; small blue windows, blue doors; schist flags, white paving, spiral pebble mosaics; flat white roofs; plain whitewashed pillars; the great folded-arm figure, the harpist of Keros, a kernos, frying pans, obsidian cores, marble bowls. (No blue domes - they are two thousand years later.)
- MinoanTiles STYLES: athens_* / mycenae_* / ionia_* / cyclades_* (palace, warehouse, temple); CAP_WALL for each set. The generator's seeds are now crc32 (Python's hash() changed every run - the art would have redrawn itself differently each time).
- The first pass's recolouring (BuildingLook) no longer applies over a culture's own art.

People - tools/empire_citizens.py: the head generator is general now (head_side / head_front / head_back from a species' parameters: snout, skull, teeth or beak, eye size, crest kind - horsehair, feathers, dome, tube, sail). Rigs art/athenian (an owl-eyed feathered raptor, white and blue), art/mycenaean (a pachycephalosaur, gold with a dark-red studded dome), art/ionian (a parasaurolophus, lapis with a gold crest), art/cycladic (a spinosaur, white with obsidian spines) - 16 frames each. surface_props CULTURE_CITIZENS: role and names for each (Athenian citizen / Mycenaean warrior / Ionian scholar / Islander). The species are my choice (only Sparta's was asked for) - easy to change in the spec.

Furniture - tools/empire_furniture.py: art/furniture/athens, mycenae, ionia, cyclades (44 pictures each): the shared forms in each culture's materials, and its own pieces - a marble chair with the owl, Athena, papyrus scrolls, a meander rug, black-figure jars (Athens); a gold-inlaid throne, the boar's-tusk helmet, a gold-and-red rug (Mycenae); a lapis chair, a seated sage, a scroll library, a star-map rug (Ionia); a whitewashed bench-seat, a folded-arm figure, a spiral rug, marble bowls (the Cyclades).

## 2026-11-13 - Every character drawn procedurally, as vectors you edit in the SVG Editor
Asked: "make all npc sprites completely procedural generated including the player sprite, if there are reference images already use them as a guide" then "make the new procedural sprites with vector graphics that can be edited via the talos svg editor, make the editor to have access to those sprites easily so i can modify them on the fly".

Done:
- tools/procedural_characters.py (new): a puppet renderer. A character is a description (build, materials, chest plate and emblem, skirt, cape, belt, back shield, head, weapon); each pose a 3D skeleton (hips, chest, shoulders, elbows, hands, knees, feet; the weapon's two ends) - rifle idle / raise1 / raise2 / aim, bow idle / drawn, labrys idle / raised / blow, a staff - turned to the 8 views and projected (the camera looking a little down); parts drawn back to front by depth: cape, tapered limbs (thigh, shin, boot, foot, knee; upper arm, forearm, bracer, hand), skirt, the torso as shaded faces (chest, waist, hips), plates, emblem, belt, shoulders, the weapon, the head. BULK 1.45: as broad as the painted originals (130 px wide vs 155).
- Heads: dinosaurs from empire_citizens.head (species parameters), a triceratops frill painted with spirals and horns, a raider's tricorne, an android's visor helmet, Kilon's hood with two points of light.
- The cast (12 rigs, 208 frames), each modelled on its painted original (kept in external/reference_sprites/<rig>/ - 8.3 MB, not in the build): player (white ceramic, red plates, visor, rifle), guard (triceratops, cream and red), android_rifle / android_bow / android_axe (cream and bronze, red capes, triceratops), pirate (crimson coat, tricorne, raptor grin, 4 poses), kilon (grey coat, hood, staff), spartan / athenian / mycenaean / ionian / cycladic (their gear and colours, their species). Every rig's frames share one page height and its feet anchors are exact (<rig>_anchors.json).
- Vector: tools/svg_draw.py (new) - an ImageDraw-like surface that records SVG shapes (polygon, line, polyline, ellipse, arcs, rects), each named by the part drawing it. Each frame is art/<rig>/svg/<rig>_<pose>_<view>.svg (page = the frame; a translate group - SvgDoc reads a viewBox's size, not its corner); the svg folders have .gdignore.
- Rasterising: scripts/sprite_sources.gd (new, SpriteSources) - the sources, their PNGs, Godot's own SVG rasteriser; tools/svg_sprites.gd rasterises all (or the changed ones).
- The SVG Editor: a "Sprites" button (Ctrl+Shift+O) - a searchable tree of every character / pose / view with thumbnails, double-click to open; saving one of them rasterises it again and swaps it into the running game (SheetPuppet.replace: runtime overrides, every puppet of that rig redrawn). Run from the project, puppets of vector rigs read their PNGs from disk (no re-import needed after an edit).
- Verified live: the Sprites list, a Spartan frame opened as 143 named objects, an edit saved -> PNG redrawn and swapped in (then restored).

Numbers: 12 rigs, 208 SVG frames, ~140 shapes each; generation ~1 min, rasterising 208 frames a few seconds.
FPS (quiet machine, everything from today included): all 91 scenarios at 240+, none under its baseline.
Tests: tests/test_vector_sprites.gd (every frame has its SVG; SvgDoc reads them, named parts; they rasterise to their picture's size; a saved sprite shows at once; the SVG Editor lists every character). test_surface updated (textures loaded from disk carry their file in resource_name; the pirate's feet anchor bound 0.15 - the procedural rifle reaches further). 246 pass.
Docs: editor.md (the game's sprites in the SVG Editor; Ctrl+Shift+O).
Caveats: simpler and flatter than the painted originals (by design, editable); running procedural_characters.py again replaces hand edits; Kilon's dialogue portrait is still the painted one.

## 2026-11-13 - Fixed: a destroyed station's trader stalled the galaxy's trade after loading a save
Asked: "did i crash?" - no; but the log showed "Invalid access to property or key 'keros:1'" (galaxy.gd _depart) repeating every frame. A trader in the save was docked at a Keros station destroyed in a war: destroying a station during play moves its traders on, but loading a save removed destroyed stations without doing so. The stranded trader failed to depart every frame - and as only one trader departs a frame (spreading the cost) and it was always first in line, no trader anywhere in the galaxy departed after the load.
Done: Galaxy._rehome_traders(station, system) (the moving-on that destroy_station did, now shared); loading a save calls it for each destroyed station, then for any trader still pointing at a station that's gone; _depart drops a trader whose station no longer exists instead of failing. Hot-reloaded into the running game: the errors stopped.
Tests: test_saves.test_traders_of_a_destroyed_station. All pass.
Files: scripts/galaxy.gd, tests/test_saves.gd.
